Originally published December 2025. ## Executive Summary This report provides a comprehensive, in-depth comparison of the pricing models for four leading AI chatbot/service APIs, updated as of February 2026: X.AI’s Grok (the AI platform developed by Elon Musk’s xAI in partnership with the X platform), Google’s Gemini, [OpenAI’s ChatGPT](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/chatgpt-ads-economic-analysis) (AI services based on GPT language models), and Anthropic’s Claude. Pricing for these services is primarily usage-based

(per token) and varies widely. For example, xAI’s **Grok 4.1** models charge only **$0.20** per 1 million input tokens and **$0.50** per 1 million output tokens ( [\[1\]](https://docs.x.ai/docs/models#:~:text=Model%20%20,%243.00%2415.00 "Highlights: Model ,$3.00$15.00")), whereas OpenAI’s flagship **GPT-5.2** is priced at **$1.75** per 1 M input and **$14.00** per 1 M output tokens. [Google’s **Gemini 3.1 Pro**](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/gemini-3-healthcare-applications) leads the current generation at **$2.00** input and **$12.00** output (per million), while **Gemini 3 Flash** offers a budget option at **$0.50/$3.00**. [Anthropic’s Claude](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/claude-opus-4-5-healthcare-pharma-ai) flagship **Claude

Opus 4.6** costs **$5.00** input and **$25.00** output per million tokens. Its mid-tier **Sonnet 4.6** is **$3/$15** (input/output) per million, and **Haiku 4.5** is **$1/$5**. Beyond per-token rates, pricing structures include subscription tiers and enterprise plans. [OpenAI](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/oracle-openai-300b-deal-analysis) offers ChatGPT Plus at $20/mo and Pro at $200/mo ( [\[2\]](https://www.reuters.com/technology/openai-projected-least-220-million-people-will-pay-chatgpt-by-2030-information-2025-11-26/#:~:text=OpenAI%20estimates%20that%20by%202030%2C,of%20its%20active%20user%20base "Highlights: OpenAI estimates that by 2030,,of its active user base")), Anthropic has a $20/mo Pro (≈$17/mo annual) plan and introduced a “Max” plan at $200/mo for heavy users ( [\[3\]](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/anthropic-intensifies-ai-competition-with-200-plan-claude-models-2025-04-09/#:~:text=times%20the%20usage%20of%20the,services%20to%20attract%20power%20users "Highlights: times

the usage of the,services to attract power users")) ( [\[4\]](https://claude-ai.chat/pricing/#:~:text=,ideal%20for%20professionals%20who%20regularly "Highlights: ,ideal for professionals who regularly")), and X’s **Premium+** tier ($22/mo) includes Grok access ( [\[5\]](https://www.reuters.com/technology/elon-musks-x-lifts-price-premium-plus-tier-pay-creators-2024-12-23/#:~:text=Elon%20Musk%27s%20social%20media%20platform,the%20Grok%20AI%20chatbot%2C%20and "Highlights: Elon Musk's social media platform,the Grok AI chatbot, and")). Google rolled out **Gemini Enterprise** (a business subscription) at $30 per user per month ( [\[6\]](https://www.axios.com/2025/10/09/google-gemini-enterprise-subscription#:~:text=one%20platform,use%20AI%20solutions "Highlights: one platform,use AI solutions")). Notably, companies have offered promotional and special pricing: e.g. US federal agencies can license Grok 4 models for only $0.42 **per agency** (per

year) under a OneGov program ( [\[7\]](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/musks-xai-provide-grok-chatbot-us-federal-agencies-2025-09-25/#:~:text=more%20AI%20into%20operations%20under,that%20meet%20federal%20security%20standards "Highlights: more AI into operations under,that meet federal security standards")) ( [\[8\]](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/elon-musks-grok-ai-to-be-used-by-us-government-at-a-price-of-42-cents-per-agency-trump-admin-joining-meta-openai-in-recent-trend-of-ai-govt-contracts#:~:text=The%20U,productivity%20using%20advanced%20AI%20tools "Highlights: The U,productivity using advanced AI tools")), and India’s Jio users received 18 months of **free** Gemini 2.5 Pro (valued at ~$399) in a 2025 partnership ( [\[9\]](https://www.reuters.com/world/india/indias-reliance-jio-users-get-18-month-free-access-googles-gemini-ai-pro-2025-10-30/#:~:text=Reliance%20Industries%20and%20Google%20announced,to%20offer%20free%20premium%20access "Highlights: Reliance Industries and Google announced,to offer free premium access")). These pricing differences have broad implications. Lower costs (like with Grok) may spur adoption by cost-sensitive developers or government, but also raise questions

about product maturity and content reliability ( [\[10\]](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/musks-xai-provide-grok-chatbot-us-federal-agencies-2025-09-25/#:~:text=Despite%20the%20cost,to%20agencies%20at%20no%20cost "Highlights: Despite the cost,to agencies at no cost")) ( [\[11\]](https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/global-bean-counters-are-struggling-to-find-value-for-money-in-anything-ai-and-that-is-a-big-big-problem#:~:text=A%20recent%20global%20study%20by,and%20new%20revenue%20management%20tools "Highlights: A recent global study by,and new revenue management tools")). Higher-cost models like Claude Opus 4.6 promise state-of-the-art performance but at a premium. The rapid evolution and competitive pressures are already being felt: AI providers continue to revisit their pricing, while customers (especially enterprises) demand transparent, flexible, usage-based models ( [\[12\]](https://www.techradar.com/pro/will-xs-usage-based-api-pricing-succeed-in-winning-over-developers#:~:text=X%20has%20introduced%20a%20new,for%20selected%20participants%E2%80%94support%20the%20shift "Highlights: X has introduced a new,for selected participants—support the shift")) (

[\[11\]](https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/global-bean-counters-are-struggling-to-find-value-for-money-in-anything-ai-and-that-is-a-big-big-problem#:~:text=A%20recent%20global%20study%20by,and%20new%20revenue%20management%20tools "Highlights: A recent global study by,and new revenue management tools")). This report examines the historical context, current pricing details, **comparative analysis**, real-world [case studies](https://intuitionlabs.ai/resources/case-studies), and future outlook, drawing on official documentation and industry sources. All claims are backed by credible references. ## Introduction and Background Since 2022, generative AI chatbots have exploded in capability and popularity, driven by models like OpenAI’s GPT series, Google DeepMind’s Gemini, Anthropic’s Claude, and, as of late 2023, Elon Musk’s xAI “Grok.” Each platform

targets developers, enterprises, and end-users with conversational AI and multimodal services. Understanding **how much these services cost** is critical for budgeting and adoption. Unlike traditional software, [AI models](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/mistral-large-3-moe-llm-explained) are typically billed on a _per-token_ or _per-use_ basis: developers pay for the amount of text (or images/audio) processed. Thus, even small differences in token rates or model capabilities can translate into large cost differences at scale. This report focuses on **API pricing** (i.e. developer/enterprise usage pricing), as well as notable subscription

tiers. We compare X.AI Grok, Google Gemini, OpenAI ChatGPT (GPT), and Anthropic Claude. Each has its own pricing page or announcements with updated rates. Costs are measured in tokens (roughly 4 characters per token), with input and output priced separately.
